intro: At B1 you linked ideas with **although**, **However,**, **because of**, **due to** and **so that**. For essays, reports and work emails you need a few more precise linkers: **whereas** and **nevertheless** for contrast, **despite** + a noun, **as** and **consequently** for cause and result, and **moreover** to add a point. You'll also learn to build a clear paragraph with them, and the trick that makes it easy: let the grammar choose the linker.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line from b1-linkers-contrast-purpose (don't re-teach it): although / even though + subject + verb, However, at the start of a new sentence with a comma, because + subject + verb vs because of / due to + noun, so that / in order to for purpose, and one linker per sentence. The key idea of this lesson: many B2 linkers mean almost the same, so GRAMMAR decides. Three kinds: (1) conjunctions that join two clauses inside one sentence + subject + verb: although, even though, whereas, while, as, since, because; (2) prepositions + a noun phrase or -ing: despite, in spite of, because of, due to, in addition to, as a result of; (3) sentence linkers that start a new sentence (or follow a semicolon) with a comma after them: however, nevertheless, nonetheless, consequently, as a result, therefore, moreover, furthermore, in addition, what's more. Explain 'clause' (subject + verb: it rained, Budi drives), 'noun phrase' (a kata benda with its little words: the heavy rain) and 'semicolon' (titik koma) the first time. Always ask: what comes after the gap, and is there a full stop or semicolon before it?

Contrast. whereas / while (sedangkan) + subject + verb compare two different facts side by side: Rina takes the KRL, whereas Budi drives (comma before them in the middle; whereas is more formal). while also means 'saat / sambil' (time): don't test that meaning. Nevertheless, / Nonetheless, (namun demikian / meskipun begitu) work like However, but are more formal and mean 'still true after what I just said' (concession): The hotel was expensive. Nevertheless, we stayed there again. For a plain comparison of two facts, use whereas or However, not Nevertheless. despite / in spite of (+ noun phrase or -ing) = meskipun before a noun: despite the traffic, in spite of feeling ill (the -ing person is the subject of the main clause). The node's common errors: *'Despite of the traffic' (mixing despite and in spite of); *'Despite it rained' (Indonesian meskipun takes anything) → Although it rained / Despite the rain / Despite the fact that it rained (teach 'despite the fact that' as a phrase to remember); *'Although it was raining, but we went out' (Meskipun …, tetapi …).

Cause and result. as / since + subject + verb = because, often at the start for a reason the reader knows or can guess: As it was late, we took an ojek. Warn that since also means 'sejak' (since 2020) and as also means 'sebagai / saat': only the reason meaning is taught here. Result: Consequently, (formal), As a result, (neutral), Therefore, (formal) = akibatnya / oleh karena itu / sehingga: a new sentence + comma, or after a semicolon (; as a result,). They can't join two clauses with only a comma like so: *'It rained, consequently we stayed in.' 'as a result' starts a new sentence; 'as a result of' + noun (As a result of the flood, …). 'therefore' in the middle (It is therefore important …, and therefore …) is correct: accept it, don't test it. Indonesian trap: 'Karena …, sehingga …' → *'Because …, so …': one linker.

Addition and register. Moreover, / Furthermore, (formal), In addition, (neutral to formal; in addition to + noun / -ing) and What's more, (neutral, common in speech and less formal writing) = selain itu / lagi pula: they add a point in the SAME direction, never a contrast (*'It saves time. Moreover, many people feel lonely' → However / Nevertheless). Register (ragam: how formal you sound) at B2 is a tendency, so test only clear cases: Moreover in a WhatsApp to a friend sounds stiff, Plus, / So at the start of an essay sentence sounds too casual; in formal writing 'also' usually goes inside the sentence (It is also cheaper). Formal ↔ everyday: moreover ↔ also / plus, consequently / therefore ↔ so, nevertheless ↔ but / still, whereas ↔ but / while. Indonesian school essays often start every sentence with Selain itu / Oleh karena itu / Namun: in English one linker every two or three sentences is enough. No British/American difference to teach here.

Organising a paragraph (builds on the topic sentences in b1-writing-stories-articles: kalimat utama, paragraf deduktif). Order: topic sentence (the main idea, not too narrow or broad) → support (2–4 sentences: facts, reasons, examples, numbers, with linkers that show the direction: For example, / First, / Moreover, / As a result,) → a turn if needed (However, / Nevertheless,) → concluding sentence (the main idea again in new words, often Overall, …; no new idea). A sentence that starts with Moreover, As a result, For example or Nevertheless can't open a paragraph: those words point back. In conclusion / To sum up usually start the last paragraph of an essay: accept them at the end of a paragraph, but teach Overall. Common errors: no topic sentence, a linker that doesn't match the logic (Moreover before a disadvantage), a new idea in the conclusion, a linker in every sentence.

Grammar limits: A0–B1 grammar plus this lesson. No participle clauses (Having finished …), no non-defining relative clauses (…, which …), no third conditional, wish or inversion (Not only … but also …). Present / past simple passive is fine but keep it rare. Don't teach hence, thus, on the other hand, besides, even so or though at the end of a sentence: if the learner uses them correctly, accept them and say hence / thus are very formal. Contexts: campus essays, company reports, work emails, news, Jakarta commuting (KRL, MRT, ojek online), startups. Correct one thing at a time, usually despite + clause, a comma-only sentence linker, or a linker with the wrong meaning.

keyPoints.title: Contrast, cause, result and addition: let the grammar choose
keyPoints.explanation: Look at what comes after the linker. A subject + verb → although, whereas, while (contrast) or as, since (reason). A noun or -ing → despite, in spite of (never 'despite of', never 'despite it rained'). A new sentence or a semicolon, with a comma after the linker → Nevertheless, (contrast), Consequently, / As a result, / Therefore, (result), Moreover, / Furthermore, / In addition, (addition). Moreover, consequently and nevertheless are formal; also, so and but are everyday.

examples.en: Rina takes the KRL to work, whereas Budi drives.
examples.id: Rina naik KRL ke kantor, sedangkan Budi menyetir.

examples.en: In spite of feeling ill, Sari finished the report.
examples.id: Meskipun tidak enak badan, Sari menyelesaikan laporannya.

examples.en: The app crashed during the sale. As a result, thousands of orders failed.
examples.id: Aplikasinya error saat promo. Akibatnya, ribuan pesanan gagal.

id.title: Kontras, sebab, akibat dan tambahan: biarkan tata bahasa yang memilih
id.explanation: Lihat apa yang datang setelah kata penghubungnya. Subjek + kata kerja → although, whereas, while (kontras) atau as, since (alasan). Kata benda atau -ing → despite, in spite of (bukan 'despite of', bukan 'despite it rained'). Kalimat baru atau titik koma, dengan koma setelah kata penghubungnya → Nevertheless, (kontras), Consequently, / As a result, / Therefore, (akibat), Moreover, / Furthermore, / In addition, (tambahan). Moreover, consequently dan nevertheless itu formal; also, so dan but untuk sehari-hari.

keyPoints.title: A clear paragraph: topic sentence → support → conclusion
keyPoints.explanation: Start with the topic sentence (the main idea). Then support it with facts, reasons and examples, and use linkers to show how each sentence connects: For example, Moreover, As a result, and Nevertheless, for a turn. End with a concluding sentence that repeats the main idea in new words (Overall, …), with no new idea. A paragraph never opens with Moreover, As a result or For example: they point back to something before.

examples.en: Working from home has clear benefits for both workers and companies.
examples.id: Bekerja dari rumah punya manfaat yang jelas bagi pekerja maupun perusahaan.

examples.en: Moreover, many of them find it easier to concentrate at home.
examples.id: Selain itu, banyak dari mereka merasa lebih mudah berkonsentrasi di rumah.

examples.en: Overall, a mix of home and office work seems to suit most people.
examples.id: Secara keseluruhan, campuran kerja dari rumah dan kantor tampaknya cocok untuk kebanyakan orang.

id.title: Paragraf yang jelas: topic sentence → pendukung → penutup
id.explanation: Mulai dengan topic sentence (kalimat utama: ide pokoknya). Lalu dukung dengan fakta, alasan dan contoh, dan pakai kata penghubung untuk menunjukkan hubungan tiap kalimat: For example, Moreover, As a result, dan Nevertheless, untuk sisi sebaliknya. Akhiri dengan kalimat penutup yang mengulang ide pokok dengan kata-kata baru (Overall, …), tanpa ide baru. Paragraf tidak pernah dibuka dengan Moreover, As a result atau For example: kata-kata itu merujuk ke sesuatu sebelumnya.

guidedPractice.prompt: although or despite? ___ having a fever, Budi gave the presentation to the client.
expected: despite
in spite of
guidedPractice.hint: After the gap comes -ing (having a fever), not a subject + verb. although needs a subject + verb (although he had a fever).

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Despite the meeting was long, nobody left early.
expected: although the meeting was long nobody left early
even though the meeting was long nobody left early
despite the long meeting nobody left early
in spite of the long meeting nobody left early
despite the fact that the meeting was long nobody left early
nobody left early although the meeting was long
nobody left early despite the long meeting
guidedPractice.hint: the meeting was long has a subject + verb, so despite can't stay with it. Use although, or make a noun: the long meeting.

guidedPractice.prompt: whereas or nevertheless? My brother loves spicy food, ___ my sister can't eat anything spicy.
expected: whereas
while
guidedPractice.hint: The gap is inside one sentence, before a subject + verb (my sister can't eat), and it compares two people. Nevertheless needs a new sentence.

guidedPractice.prompt: as or as a result? The flood closed the main road. ___, many students missed the exam.
expected: as a result
guidedPractice.hint: Full stop before the gap, comma after it: a new sentence that gives the result. as needs a subject + verb after it in the same sentence.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which sentence usually comes first in an English paragraph: the topic sentence, a supporting sentence or the concluding sentence?
expected: the topic sentence
topic sentence
guidedPractice.hint: The first sentence gives the main idea (kalimat utama), like a paragraf deduktif.

independentPractice.prompt: Join the two sentences with whereas: Rina prefers working from home. Budi prefers the office.
expected: rina prefers working from home whereas budi prefers the office
budi prefers the office whereas rina prefers working from home
whereas rina prefers working from home budi prefers the office
whereas budi prefers the office rina prefers working from home
independentPractice.hint: whereas + subject + verb compares two facts in one sentence. Put a comma before whereas.

independentPractice.prompt: Add the second point with Furthermore, as in a formal report: The new app is cheaper. It is easier to use.
expected: the new app is cheaper furthermore it is easier to use
the new app is cheaper furthermore its easier to use
the new app is cheaper furthermore it is also easier to use
independentPractice.hint: Furthermore starts the second sentence, with a comma after it: … cheaper. Furthermore, it …

independentPractice.prompt: Write the word that often starts a concluding sentence at the end of a paragraph (it means secara keseluruhan).
expected: overall
independentPractice.hint: It starts with O and has a comma after it: ___, a mix of home and office work suits most people.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Despite of the power cut, the hospital kept working normally.
acceptableAnswers: despite the power cut the hospital kept working normally
in spite of the power cut the hospital kept working normally
the hospital kept working normally despite the power cut
the hospital kept working normally in spite of the power cut
although there was a power cut the hospital kept working normally
even though there was a power cut the hospital kept working normally
assessment.rubric: Correct: Despite the power cut, the hospital kept working normally (despite + noun, no of) or In spite of the power cut, …. 'Although there was a power cut, …' = 100 (although + subject + verb). 'In spite the power cut' = 30 (of missing). 'Although the power cut, …' = 20 (although needs a subject + verb). Unchanged 'Despite of' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with despite: Although it rained heavily, the festival in Bandung continued.
acceptableAnswers: despite the heavy rain the festival in bandung continued
despite heavy rain the festival in bandung continued
the festival in bandung continued despite the heavy rain
the festival in bandung continued despite heavy rain
despite the fact that it rained heavily the festival in bandung continued
the festival in bandung continued despite the fact that it rained heavily
despite it raining heavily the festival in bandung continued
the festival in bandung continued despite it raining heavily
despite the very heavy rain the festival in bandung continued
assessment.rubric: Correct: Despite the heavy rain, the festival in Bandung continued (despite + a noun phrase), or Despite the fact that it rained heavily, …. 'Despite the rain, …' = 80 (right pattern, but 'heavily' is lost). 'In spite of the heavy rain' = 80 (right, but the task said despite). 'Despite it rained heavily' = 0 (despite can't take a subject + verb: the node's common error). 'Despite of the heavy rain' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Write whereas, nevertheless or despite: In Jakarta, most people get to work by car or motorbike, ___ in Tokyo most people take the train.
acceptableAnswers: whereas
while
assessment.rubric: Correct: whereas (inside one sentence, + subject + verb, comparing two different facts). 'while' = 100 (same meaning here). 'nevertheless' = 0 (it starts a new sentence and means 'still true despite that', not a comparison). 'despite' = 0 (it needs a noun or -ing, not a subject + verb). 'but' = 50 (grammatical, but not one of the choices and less precise).

assessment.prompt: Write as, consequently or due to: Sales of the company's old phone model fell sharply last year. ___, the company stopped making it.
acceptableAnswers: consequently
as a result
therefore
assessment.rubric: Correct: Consequently (a full stop before the gap and a comma after it: a new sentence that gives the result). 'As a result' or 'Therefore' = 100 (also right). 'as' = 0 (it needs a subject + verb in the same sentence and gives a reason, not a result). 'due to' = 0 (it needs a noun after it). 'So' = 50 (the right idea, but too casual for this sentence and not one of the choices).

assessment.prompt: This short paragraph is about the good and bad sides of online classes. One linker is wrong for the meaning. Write the linker that should replace it (one word): 'Online classes save students a lot of travel time and money. Moreover, many students find it hard to stay motivated without their classmates.'
acceptableAnswers: however
nevertheless
nonetheless
assessment.rubric: Correct: However (or Nevertheless / Nonetheless): the second sentence gives a disadvantage after an advantage, so it needs a contrast linker; Moreover only adds a point in the same direction. 'On the other hand' = 90 (right meaning, but not one word). 'But' = 60 (right meaning, informal at the start of a sentence in an essay). 'Furthermore', 'In addition' or 'As a result' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Put the sentences in the best order to make one paragraph. Write the four letters in order. A: Overall, online courses are a smart choice for busy office workers. B: Online English courses have several advantages for people with full-time jobs. C: Furthermore, they are usually cheaper than classes at a language school. D: First, you can study at any time, even on the KRL home.
acceptableAnswers: b d c a
bdca
assessment.rubric: Correct: B D C A (B = topic sentence with the main idea; D = the first advantage; C = Furthermore adds a second one; A = Overall closes with the main idea in new words). 'B C D A' = 50 (topic sentence and conclusion right, but First must come before Furthermore). Any order that doesn't start with B or doesn't end with A = 0 (a paragraph can't open with First, Furthermore or Overall).

assessment.prompt: Read the paragraph and choose the best concluding sentence. Write A, B or C. 'The new MRT line has made life easier for many commuters in Jakarta. Journeys that took 90 minutes by car now take about 30. In addition, the trains are clean, cool and on time. Nevertheless, tickets are still too expensive for some workers.' A: My cousin lives near Bundaran HI. B: Overall, the MRT is a big step forward, although the fares need to come down. C: For example, trains come every few minutes at rush hour.
acceptableAnswers: b
sentence b
assessment.rubric: Correct: B (Overall + the main idea in new words, and it also sums up the turn about the price). A = 0 (a new idea that doesn't belong to the paragraph). C = 0 (a supporting detail: For example points back and can't close the paragraph).

material.title: What comes after it? Three kinds of linker

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: **although** + subject + verb, **However,** at the start of a new sentence, **because** + subject + verb but **because of / due to** + a noun, and only **one linker per sentence**.

At B2 you'll meet many new linkers, and several of them mean almost the same. So the easiest way to choose is **grammar**: look at **what comes after the linker** and **where it stands**.
- **Kind 1: + subject + verb, inside one sentence.** A **clause** = a subject (who or what: *it, Budi, the meeting*) + a verb (*rained, drives, was*). *although, even though, whereas, while, as, since, because*.
- **Kind 2: + a noun or -ing.** A **noun phrase** = a noun (kata benda) with its little words: *the heavy rain, a long meeting*; or a verb + -ing: *feeling tired*. *despite, in spite of, because of, due to, in addition to, as a result of*.
- **Kind 3: starts a new sentence**, after a full stop or a **semicolon** (`;`, titik koma), **with a comma after it**. *However, Nevertheless, Nonetheless, Consequently, As a result, Therefore, Moreover, Furthermore, In addition, What's more*. Like *However*, they can't join two clauses with only a comma.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari B1: **although** + subjek + kata kerja, **However,** di awal kalimat baru, **because** + subjek + kata kerja tapi **because of / due to** + kata benda, dan hanya **satu kata penghubung per kalimat**.

Di B2 kamu akan bertemu banyak kata penghubung (linker) baru, dan beberapa artinya hampir sama. Jadi cara termudah untuk memilih adalah **tata bahasa**: lihat **apa yang datang setelah kata penghubungnya** dan **di mana posisinya**.
- **Jenis 1: + subjek + kata kerja, di dalam satu kalimat.** **Klausa** (clause) = subjek (siapa atau apa: *it, Budi, the meeting*) + kata kerja (*rained, drives, was*). *although, even though, whereas, while, as, since, because*.
- **Jenis 2: + kata benda atau -ing.** **Frasa kata benda** (noun phrase) = kata benda dengan kata-kata kecil di sekitarnya: *the heavy rain, a long meeting*; atau kata kerja + -ing: *feeling tired*. *despite, in spite of, because of, due to, in addition to, as a result of*.
- **Jenis 3: memulai kalimat baru**, setelah titik atau **titik koma** (`;`), **dengan koma setelahnya**. *However, Nevertheless, Nonetheless, Consequently, As a result, Therefore, Moreover, Furthermore, In addition, What's more*. Sama seperti *However*, kata-kata ini tidak bisa menyambung dua klausa hanya dengan koma.

rows.id: Meskipun hujannya deras, konsernya tetap berlangsung.

rows.en: The rain was heavy; nevertheless, the concert went ahead.
rows.id: Hujannya deras; namun demikian, konsernya tetap berlangsung.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: **one Indonesian word, several English kinds.** *meskipun* → **although** (+ subject + verb) or **despite** (+ noun). *karena* → **because / as / since** (+ subject + verb) or **because of / due to** (+ noun). *sehingga / akibatnya* → **so** (inside one sentence) or **As a result, / Consequently,** (a new sentence). So translate the **grammar**, not just the word: first look at what comes next.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **satu kata Indonesia, beberapa jenis dalam bahasa Inggris.** *meskipun* → **although** (+ subjek + kata kerja) atau **despite** (+ kata benda). *karena* → **because / as / since** (+ subjek + kata kerja) atau **because of / due to** (+ kata benda). *sehingga / akibatnya* → **so** (di dalam satu kalimat) atau **As a result, / Consequently,** (kalimat baru). Jadi terjemahkan **tata bahasanya**, bukan hanya katanya: lihat dulu apa yang datang berikutnya.

blocks.prompt: Which word fits the gap? The meeting was very long; ___, nobody looked tired.
blocks.explain: There's a semicolon before the gap and a comma after it, so you need a kind-3 linker: **however**. *although* needs a subject + verb right after it, with no comma, and *despite* needs a noun or -ing.

id.prompt: Kata mana yang cocok? The meeting was very long; ___, nobody looked tired.
id.explain: Ada titik koma sebelum titik-titiknya dan koma setelahnya, jadi kamu butuh kata penghubung jenis 3: **however**. *although* butuh subjek + kata kerja tepat setelahnya, tanpa koma, dan *despite* butuh kata benda atau -ing.

id.title: Apa yang datang setelahnya? Tiga jenis kata penghubung

blocks.text:
**whereas / while** (= *sedangkan*) + subject + verb compare **two different facts** side by side: *Rina takes the KRL to work, **whereas** Budi drives.* In the middle of a sentence, put a comma before them. *whereas* is more formal; *while* is common in speech and writing. (Careful: *while* also means *saat / sambil*: *I read while I wait for the train.* Here we only use it to compare.)

**Nevertheless, / Nonetheless,** (= *namun demikian / meskipun begitu*) work like **However,**: a new sentence (or after `;`) with a comma. They're more formal, and they mean 'this is **still** true, even after what I just said': *The hotel was expensive. **Nevertheless,** we stayed there again.* For a plain comparison (Rina vs Budi), use *whereas* or *However*, not *Nevertheless*.

**despite / in spite of** (= *meskipun*, before a noun) + a **noun phrase** or **-ing**: *despite the traffic*, *in spite of feeling ill*. With -ing, the person is the subject of the sentence: *In spite of feeling ill, **Sari** finished the report* (Sari felt ill). They mean the same; *in spite of* is a little less formal.

Need a subject + verb? Use **although**, or the phrase **despite the fact that** + subject + verb (a phrase to remember).

id.text:
**whereas / while** (= *sedangkan*) + subjek + kata kerja membandingkan **dua fakta yang berbeda** berdampingan: *Rina takes the KRL to work, **whereas** Budi drives.* (Rina naik KRL ke kantor, sedangkan Budi menyetir.) Di tengah kalimat, beri koma sebelumnya. *whereas* lebih formal; *while* umum dipakai dalam percakapan maupun tulisan. (Hati-hati: *while* juga berarti *saat / sambil*: *I read while I wait for the train.* Di sini kita hanya memakainya untuk membandingkan.)

**Nevertheless, / Nonetheless,** (= *namun demikian / meskipun begitu*) bekerja seperti **However,**: kalimat baru (atau setelah `;`) dengan koma. Keduanya lebih formal, dan artinya 'hal ini **tetap** benar, walaupun ada yang baru saja saya katakan': *The hotel was expensive. **Nevertheless,** we stayed there again.* (Hotelnya mahal. Namun demikian, kami menginap di sana lagi.) Untuk perbandingan biasa (Rina vs Budi), pakai *whereas* atau *However*, bukan *Nevertheless*.

**despite / in spite of** (= *meskipun*, sebelum kata benda) + **frasa kata benda** atau **-ing**: *despite the traffic*, *in spite of feeling ill*. Dengan -ing, orangnya adalah subjek kalimat: *In spite of feeling ill, **Sari** finished the report* (Sari yang tidak enak badan). Artinya sama; *in spite of* sedikit kurang formal.

Butuh subjek + kata kerja? Pakai **although**, atau frasa **despite the fact that** + subjek + kata kerja (frasa untuk diingat saja).

rows.note: despite the fact that + subject + verb

id.note: despite the fact that + subjek + kata kerja

blocks.text:
Three classic mistakes:
- `Despite of the traffic, we arrived on time` ✗. It's **despite** or **in spite of**, never *despite of* (people mix the two): *Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.*
- `Despite it rained, the event continued` ✗. In Indonesian, *walaupun hujan* can take anything, but **despite** can't take a subject + verb. Say *Although it rained, …*, *Despite the rain, …* or *Despite the fact that it rained, …*.
- `Although it was raining, but we went out` ✗ (*Meskipun …, tetapi …*). Still one linker per sentence, also with despite and whereas.

id.text:
Tiga kesalahan klasik:
- `Despite of the traffic, we arrived on time` ✗. Yang benar **despite** atau **in spite of**, tidak pernah *despite of* (orang sering mencampur keduanya): *Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.*
- `Despite it rained, the event continued` ✗. Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *walaupun hujan* bisa diikuti apa saja, tapi **despite** tidak bisa diikuti subjek + kata kerja. Katakan *Although it rained, …*, *Despite the rain, …* atau *Despite the fact that it rained, …*.
- `Although it was raining, but we went out` ✗ (*Meskipun …, tetapi …*). Tetap satu kata penghubung per kalimat, juga dengan despite dan whereas.

options: Despite of the long queue, we got our tickets.
Despite the queue was long, we got our tickets.
Despite the long queue, we got our tickets.
blocks.explain: **despite** + a noun phrase (*the long queue*), with no *of*. The first sentence adds *of* (that's *in spite of* mixed with *despite*). The second puts a subject + verb (*the queue was*) after despite: that needs **although**.

id.explain: **despite** + frasa kata benda (*the long queue*), tanpa *of*. Kalimat pertama menambahkan *of* (itu *in spite of* yang tercampur dengan *despite*). Kalimat kedua menaruh subjek + kata kerja (*the queue was*) setelah despite: itu butuh **although**.

material.title: Cause and result: as, since, consequently, as a result

blocks.text:
**Cause (the reason): as / since** + subject + verb = *because* (*karena*). They often come **first**, for a reason the reader already knows or can guess: ***As** it was late, we took an ojek home.* ***Since** you're in Bandung this week, let's have lunch.* (Careful: *since* also means *sejak*: *since 2020*; and *as* has other meanings, like *sebagai*. Here we only use them for reasons.)

**Result (what happens next): Consequently, / As a result, / Therefore,** (= *akibatnya / oleh karena itu / sehingga*). They're kind 3: a **new sentence + comma**, or after a **semicolon**: *The app crashed during the sale. **As a result,** thousands of orders failed.*
- **consequently** and **therefore** are formal (reports, essays, news); **as a result** is neutral; **so** inside one sentence (*…, so we stayed in*) is everyday.
- They can't join two clauses with only a comma like *so*: `It rained, consequently we stayed in` ✗.
- **As a result,** + a new sentence, but **as a result of** + a noun: *As a result of the flood, the road is closed.*
- You may see *therefore* in the middle (*It is therefore important to …*): that's correct too.

id.text:
**Sebab (alasannya): as / since** + subjek + kata kerja = *because* (*karena*). Keduanya sering ada **di depan**, untuk alasan yang sudah diketahui atau bisa ditebak pembaca: ***As** it was late, we took an ojek home.* (Karena sudah malam, kami naik ojek pulang.) ***Since** you're in Bandung this week, let's have lunch.* (Karena kamu di Bandung minggu ini, ayo makan siang.) (Hati-hati: *since* juga berarti *sejak*: *since 2020*; dan *as* punya arti lain, seperti *sebagai*. Di sini kita hanya memakainya untuk alasan.)

**Akibat (apa yang terjadi selanjutnya): Consequently, / As a result, / Therefore,** (= *akibatnya / oleh karena itu / sehingga*). Ini jenis 3: **kalimat baru + koma**, atau setelah **titik koma**: *The app crashed during the sale. **As a result,** thousands of orders failed.*
- **consequently** dan **therefore** formal (laporan, esai, berita); **as a result** netral; **so** di dalam satu kalimat (*…, so we stayed in*) untuk sehari-hari.
- Kata-kata ini tidak bisa menyambung dua klausa hanya dengan koma seperti *so*: `It rained, consequently we stayed in` ✗.
- **As a result,** + kalimat baru, tapi **as a result of** + kata benda: *As a result of the flood, the road is closed.*
- Kamu mungkin melihat *therefore* di tengah (*It is therefore important to …*): itu juga benar.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: **Karena …, sehingga …** → `Because the road was flooded, so we stayed home` ✗. Choose **one** linker: *Because the road was flooded, we stayed home.* / *The road was flooded, so we stayed home.* / *The road was flooded. As a result, we stayed home.* And a long Indonesian sentence with *sehingga* in the middle often works better in English as two sentences: the second one starts with **As a result,** (formal) or the first one ends with **, so …** (everyday).

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **Karena …, sehingga …** → `Because the road was flooded, so we stayed home` ✗. Pilih **satu** kata penghubung: *Because the road was flooded, we stayed home.* / *The road was flooded, so we stayed home.* / *The road was flooded. As a result, we stayed home.* Dan kalimat Indonesia yang panjang dengan *sehingga* di tengahnya sering lebih enak dalam bahasa Inggris sebagai dua kalimat: kalimat kedua dimulai dengan **As a result,** (formal), atau kalimat pertama diakhiri dengan **, so …** (sehari-hari).

blocks.prompt: Complete: Online orders doubled in December. ___, the warehouse hired 50 extra staff.
blocks.explain: A full stop before the gap and a comma after it: a new sentence that gives the **result** (more orders → more staff), so **Consequently,**. *Since* needs a subject + verb after it in the same sentence and gives a reason; *Because of* needs a noun.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Online orders doubled in December. ___, the warehouse hired 50 extra staff.
id.explain: Ada titik sebelum titik-titiknya dan koma setelahnya: kalimat baru yang memberi **akibat** (pesanan bertambah → karyawan bertambah), jadi **Consequently,**. *Since* butuh subjek + kata kerja setelahnya dalam kalimat yang sama dan memberi alasan; *Because of* butuh kata benda.

id.title: Sebab dan akibat: as, since, consequently, as a result

material.title: Adding a point, in the right style

blocks.text:
To **add** a point in the **same direction** (= *selain itu / lagi pula*), use a kind-3 linker + comma:
- **Moreover, / Furthermore,**: formal (essays, reports, formal emails).
- **In addition,**: neutral to formal. Before a noun or -ing: **in addition to** + noun / -ing: *In addition to a good salary, the job offers free training.*
- **What's more,**: neutral, common in speaking and less formal writing.
They only **add**. Never use *Moreover* for the other side of the story: that's *However, / Nevertheless,*.

**Register** (*ragam bahasa*: how formal you sound) matters at B2. The same idea:
- a report: *The plan is affordable. **Moreover,** it can start next month.*
- everyday: *The plan's cheap, and it can **also** start next month.* / WhatsApp: *It's cheap. **Plus** it can start next month!*
*Moreover* in a WhatsApp to a friend sounds stiff, and *Plus* or *So* at the start of an essay sentence sounds too casual. In formal writing, **also** usually goes **inside** the sentence (*It is **also** cheaper*), not at the start.

id.text:
Untuk **menambah** poin ke **arah yang sama** (= *selain itu / lagi pula*), pakai kata penghubung jenis 3 + koma:
- **Moreover, / Furthermore,**: formal (esai, laporan, email formal).
- **In addition,**: netral sampai formal. Sebelum kata benda atau -ing: **in addition to** + kata benda / -ing: *In addition to a good salary, the job offers free training.* (Selain gaji yang bagus, pekerjaan ini menawarkan pelatihan gratis.)
- **What's more,**: netral, umum dalam percakapan dan tulisan yang kurang formal.
Kata-kata ini hanya **menambah**. Jangan pernah pakai *Moreover* untuk sisi sebaliknya: itu tugas *However, / Nevertheless,*.

**Register** (*ragam bahasa*: seberapa formal kamu terdengar) penting di B2. Ide yang sama:
- laporan: *The plan is affordable. **Moreover,** it can start next month.*
- sehari-hari: *The plan's cheap, and it can **also** start next month.* / WhatsApp: *It's cheap. **Plus** it can start next month!*
*Moreover* di WhatsApp ke teman terdengar kaku, dan *Plus* atau *So* di awal kalimat esai terdengar terlalu santai. Dalam tulisan formal, **also** biasanya ada **di dalam** kalimat (*It is **also** cheaper*), bukan di awal.

rows.en: The proposal is affordable. Furthermore, it can start next month.
rows.id: Proposalnya terjangkau. Selain itu, proposal ini bisa dimulai bulan depan.

rows.en: In addition to a good salary, the job offers free training.
rows.id: Selain gaji yang bagus, pekerjaan ini menawarkan pelatihan gratis.

rows.id: Kafenya punya Wi-Fi cepat. Lagi pula, kopinya murah.
rows.note: What's more: neutral, a bit chatty

rows.en: The café has fast Wi-Fi, and the coffee is also cheap.
rows.id: Kafenya punya Wi-Fi cepat, dan kopinya juga murah.

blocks.text:
**Formal ↔ everyday pairs:** *moreover / furthermore* ↔ *also, plus* · *consequently / therefore* ↔ *so* · *nevertheless* ↔ *but, still* · *whereas* ↔ *but, while* · *despite* ↔ *although*.

Indonesian school essays often start **every** sentence with *Selain itu, Oleh karena itu, Namun*. In English that sounds heavy. One linker every two or three sentences is enough: use one where the link isn't obvious.

id.text:
**Pasangan formal ↔ sehari-hari:** *moreover / furthermore* ↔ *also, plus* · *consequently / therefore* ↔ *so* · *nevertheless* ↔ *but, still* · *whereas* ↔ *but, while* · *despite* ↔ *although*.

Esai sekolah di Indonesia sering memulai **setiap** kalimat dengan *Selain itu, Oleh karena itu, Namun*. Dalam bahasa Inggris itu terasa berat. Satu kata penghubung setiap dua atau tiga kalimat sudah cukup: pakai di tempat yang hubungannya tidak jelas.

blocks.prompt: Rina is writing a formal report for her manager. Which linker fits best? The new software saves time. ___ it reduces mistakes in the invoices.
blocks.explain: The second sentence adds another good point (same direction), and the report is formal: **Moreover,**. *Plus* also adds, but it's too casual for a report. *Nevertheless* is for a contrast ('still true after that'), not for adding.

id.prompt: Rina menulis laporan formal untuk manajernya. Kata penghubung mana yang paling cocok? The new software saves time. ___ it reduces mistakes in the invoices.
id.explain: Kalimat kedua menambah satu poin bagus lagi (arah yang sama), dan laporannya formal: **Moreover,**. *Plus* juga menambah, tapi terlalu santai untuk laporan. *Nevertheless* untuk kontras ('tetap benar setelah itu'), bukan untuk menambah.

id.title: Menambah poin, dengan gaya yang tepat

blocks.text:
In B1 you learnt that a paragraph has **one main idea**, usually in the first sentence: the **topic sentence** (*kalimat utama*, like a *paragraf deduktif*). At B2, build the whole paragraph in this order:
1. **Topic sentence**: the main idea, not too narrow (one detail) and not too broad.
2. **Support**: 2–4 sentences with facts, reasons, examples and numbers. Linkers show the direction: *For example, … / First, … / Moreover, … / As a result, …*
3. **A turn**, if you need one: the other side, with *However, / Nevertheless,*.
4. **Concluding sentence**: the main idea again, in new words, often with **Overall,** (*secara keseluruhan*). No new ideas here.

A sentence that starts with **Moreover, As a result, For example** or **Nevertheless** can't open a paragraph: these words point back to something that came before. (*In conclusion* and *To sum up* usually start the **last paragraph** of an essay; at the end of one paragraph, *Overall,* is enough.)

id.text:
Di B1 kamu sudah belajar bahwa satu paragraf punya **satu ide pokok**, biasanya di kalimat pertama: **topic sentence** (*kalimat utama*, seperti *paragraf deduktif*). Di B2, susun seluruh paragraf dengan urutan ini:
1. **Topic sentence**: ide pokoknya, tidak terlalu sempit (satu detail) dan tidak terlalu luas.
2. **Pendukung**: 2–4 kalimat berisi fakta, alasan, contoh dan angka. Kata penghubung menunjukkan arahnya: *For example, … / First, … / Moreover, … / As a result, …*
3. **Sisi sebaliknya**, kalau perlu: dengan *However, / Nevertheless,*.
4. **Kalimat penutup** (concluding sentence): ide pokoknya lagi, dengan kata-kata baru, sering dengan **Overall,** (*secara keseluruhan*). Tidak ada ide baru di sini.

Kalimat yang dimulai dengan **Moreover, As a result, For example** atau **Nevertheless** tidak bisa membuka paragraf: kata-kata ini merujuk ke sesuatu yang datang sebelumnya. (*In conclusion* dan *To sum up* biasanya membuka **paragraf terakhir** sebuah esai; di akhir satu paragraf, *Overall,* sudah cukup.)

blocks.text:
Check your paragraph before you send it:
- Does the **first sentence** give the main idea?
- Does **every sentence** support it? (A sentence about something else goes out.)
- Does each linker **match the logic**? Adding → *Moreover*; the other side → *However / Nevertheless*; a result → *As a result*. `It saves time. Moreover, many people feel lonely` ✗: that's the other side, so *However*.
- Is there a linker in **every** sentence? Then take some out.
- Does the last sentence **close** the idea, without a new one?

id.text:
Cek paragrafmu sebelum mengirimnya:
- Apakah **kalimat pertama** memberi ide pokoknya?
- Apakah **setiap kalimat** mendukungnya? (Kalimat tentang hal lain dikeluarkan.)
- Apakah setiap kata penghubung **cocok dengan logikanya**? Menambah → *Moreover*; sisi sebaliknya → *However / Nevertheless*; akibat → *As a result*. `It saves time. Moreover, many people feel lonely` ✗: itu sisi sebaliknya, jadi *However*.
- Apakah ada kata penghubung di **setiap** kalimat? Kalau ya, buang sebagian.
- Apakah kalimat terakhir **menutup** idenya, tanpa ide baru?

blocks.prompt: Which sentence can open a paragraph?
options: As a result, many students now study online.
Online learning has changed the way Indonesians study.
For example, many universities now offer online degrees.
blocks.explain: A paragraph opens with its **topic sentence**, the main idea: *Online learning has changed the way Indonesians study.* *As a result* and *For example* point back to something said before, so they can only come later in the paragraph.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang bisa membuka paragraf?
id.explain: Paragraf dibuka dengan **topic sentence**-nya, ide pokoknya: *Online learning has changed the way Indonesians study.* *As a result* dan *For example* merujuk ke sesuatu yang sudah disebut sebelumnya, jadi hanya bisa muncul lebih belakang di paragraf.

Halaman ini tidak membahas whereas, nevertheless, atau kata penghubung sebab, akibat dan tambahan.

resources.title: An opinion essay
resources.note: A B2 model essay with tasks. See how However, Moreover, whereas and Finally link the ideas, and how the conclusion sums up the main points without new ones. It's a whole five-paragraph essay, a step beyond one paragraph.

id.note: Contoh esai B2 dengan latihan. Lihat bagaimana However, Moreover, whereas dan Finally menghubungkan ide-idenya, dan bagaimana kesimpulannya merangkum poin utama tanpa ide baru. Ini esai utuh lima paragraf, selangkah lebih jauh dari satu paragraf.

id.intro: Di B1 kamu sudah menghubungkan ide dengan **although**, **However,**, **because of**, **due to** dan **so that**. Untuk esai, laporan dan email kantor kamu butuh beberapa kata penghubung yang lebih tepat: **whereas** dan **nevertheless** untuk kontras, **despite** + kata benda, **as** dan **consequently** untuk sebab dan akibat, dan **moreover** untuk menambah poin. Kamu juga akan belajar menyusun paragraf yang jelas dengan kata-kata itu, dan triknya supaya gampang: biarkan tata bahasa yang memilih kata penghubungnya.

assessment.lkw-1: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Despite of the power cut, the hospital kept working normally.
assessment.lkw-2: Tulis ulang kalimatnya dengan despite: Although it rained heavily, the festival in Bandung continued.
assessment.lkw-3: Tulis whereas, nevertheless atau despite: In Jakarta, most people get to work by car or motorbike, ___ in Tokyo most people take the train.
assessment.lkw-4: Tulis as, consequently atau due to: Sales of the company's old phone model fell sharply last year. ___, the company stopped making it.
assessment.lkw-5: Paragraf pendek ini tentang sisi baik dan buruk kelas online. Satu kata penghubung salah untuk maknanya. Tulis kata penghubung (satu kata, dalam bahasa Inggris) yang seharusnya menggantikannya: 'Online classes save students a lot of travel time and money. Moreover, many students find it hard to stay motivated without their classmates.'
assessment.lkw-6: Susun kalimat-kalimat ini dalam urutan terbaik menjadi satu paragraf. Tulis keempat hurufnya sesuai urutan. A: Overall, online courses are a smart choice for busy office workers. B: Online English courses have several advantages for people with full-time jobs. C: Furthermore, they are usually cheaper than classes at a language school. D: First, you can study at any time, even on the KRL home.
assessment.lkw-7: Baca paragrafnya dan pilih kalimat penutup terbaik. Tulis A, B atau C. 'The new MRT line has made life easier for many commuters in Jakarta. Journeys that took 90 minutes by car now take about 30. In addition, the trains are clean, cool and on time. Nevertheless, tickets are still too expensive for some workers.' A: My cousin lives near Bundaran HI. B: Overall, the MRT is a big step forward, although the fares need to come down. C: For example, trains come every few minutes at rush hour.
